title: Fix a Bloated, Insecure Dockerfile With a Multi-Stage Build
intro: This image is 1.1GB, runs as root, ships the whole build toolchain to production — and has a live API key baked into one of its layers.

steps.starter_content:
FROM node:20
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
ENV API_KEY=sk_live_abc123
RUN npm install
RUN npm run build
EXPOSE 3000
CMD npm start
steps.prompt: Rewrite it as a multi-stage build. Stage 1: 'FROM node:20 AS build', copy the source, 'npm ci', 'npm run build'. Stage 2: 'FROM node:20-alpine', copy ONLY the built output and dependencies from the build stage (COPY --from=build ...), run as USER node, and start with an exec-form CMD. Remove the API_KEY entirely — it must be passed at runtime instead.
steps.hint: Two FROM lines = two stages. Only the LAST stage becomes the image, so the build tools in stage 1 never ship. Pull artifacts across with e.g. COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist and COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules. Any ENV holding a secret is readable by anyone who pulls the image.
steps.solution:
FROM node:20 AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]
steps.fake_output:
[+] Building 41.8s (14/14) FINISHED

$ docker images app
REPOSITORY  TAG   SIZE
app         v2    168MB   (was 1.1GB)
steps.explanation: ~85% smaller, no compilers or source in production, non-root, and no secret in any layer.
steps.why: Smaller images pull faster (faster scaling and rollbacks) and contain fewer packages for scanners to flag. But deleting the ENV line only protects FUTURE images: the old image's layers still contain the key, readable via 'docker history' — so that key must be rotated now (same rule as cicd-incident-004: once a secret is published, removal isn't enough). Pass secrets at runtime with -e or a secrets manager, or use BuildKit '--mount=type=secret' if the build itself needs one.
